$comment: PLUGIN — how to translate the inventory into AJEAN's MCP servers.
THE ONE CLIENT WITH NO CONFIG FILE. AJEAN keeps its MCP servers in a bbolt
database (bucket 'state', key 'mcp'), not in a JSON file — read from
E:\Coding\ajean\internal\ajean\mcp_config.go on 2026-10-09. So there is
nothing to write on disk, and this plugin declares writer 'api' instead.
Why not write the database directly: bbolt takes an EXCLUSIVE file lock, and
AJEAN is normally running. At best we would block; at worst we would corrupt
a store that also holds the user's keys and tokens. The API exists for this.
THE SHAPE. Its /api/mcp/save takes ONE named server:
{"name": …, "command": …, "args": […], "env": {…},
"url": …, "headers": {…}, "enabled": true}
which is the same map our Render() produces, plus the name — so the whole
adapter is 'render, then add a name'. Transports are inferred from the
presence of 'command' or 'url': there is NO 'type' field, hence omit_type
covering both. We also never send 'enabled': its default when the key is
absent is already true, so leaving it out keeps its file clean.
CONSEQUENCE OF AN API CLIENT, worth knowing before it surprises anyone:
AJEAN MUST BE RUNNING for an apply to reach it. A file client can be
configured while closed; this one cannot. The manager says so plainly rather
than failing obscurely.
PORT: AJEAN's web server is `ajean web [port]`, default 8090. 0.0.0.0, but we
talk to it on loopback. Its /api/* is guarded by a 'web key' (Bearer) only if
one is set; none is set today, so api_auth_header is left empty.
